_note: Six metric definitions for the MiseQ v6.4 sample, drafted from the data and
verified against it (WP13.23). Every figure quoted in a caveat was computed
before the sentence was written; none is repeated from the supplied contract
without being checked. Two were confirmed against MiseQ own published numbers:
stage=prep_trim is 2,634.32 kg and waste_cause=prep_trim is 2,360.22 kg, which
is the '2,634 vs 2,360' their meta_data_quality row cites.
Not here, deliberately: waste valued in RM, and any Food Variance analogue.
The RM chain is reachable in v6.4 -- erp_ingredient_key joins fact_waste to
fact_stock_move_outlet, and move_id carries it to fact_stock_move.unit_cost,
all 46,346 rows bridging. It is left out because fact_stock_move.cost_basis is
'unknown' on all 51,356 rows: the number can be computed and every input to it
is one the source declines to vouch for. Food Variance is a different case --
it needs a theoretical-cost baseline this dataset does not contain at all, so
it is an absent concept rather than a missing table. See B-168.
Owner rule, 2026-08-28: if the number cannot be computed and checked, it is
not proposed. Owner corrections applied the same day: waste_kg's caveat says
what the number is good for rather than only what it is not, and the metric
once called avoidable_waste is edible_waste, because the old name asserted
what its own caveat retracted.
Synonyms are short phrases, not sample questions. matching() searches each
synonym as a contiguous whole-word phrase, so 'how much food are we throwing
away' only ever matches itself. The first seeding of this file was written the
wrong way and waste_by_cause matched NOTHING -- not 'what is causing our
wastage', not 'show me wastage by reason'. That is B-085 exactly, found by
running matching() against real phrasings rather than by reading the list.
edible_waste's synonyms are deliberately tighter than the rest, because it is
the one that BINDS: a false match makes the critic enforce edible_flag = 1 on
a question that was never about edibility.
carrying the 15 views. It was absent before because fact_waste has no money
column and B-162's erp_keys substitute errs -53% to +706%; v_waste_valued
supplies the chain honestly, with value_is_available as the required filter
meta_data_quality's waste_valuation_resolved row names. That row also demands
valued-row, valued-kg and category coverage be disclosed -- 7,147/11,747,
509.58/5,528.61 kg and 6/9 -- so all three are in the caveat. See B-168.
waste_value_rm was proposed on 2026-08-28 and withdrawn by the owner the same
day. v_waste_valued does supply a defensible chain -- value_is_available is
the filter meta_data_quality names, and the kg side reconciles -- but it
prices only 509.58 kg of 5,528.61, 9.2% by weight, and ayam (3,848 kg, ~70%
of all waste) is one of the three unpriced categories. So the largest part of
any waste-cost question is exactly what the number omits. Owner, 2026-08-29:
leave it out. Two days before a demo, a number whose caveat is longer than
its usefulness is not worth a screen. See B-168.

definitions.name: waste_kg
definitions.description: Food thrown away, by weight in kilograms. fact_waste.waste_kg is already the portion-to-kilogram conversion: it agrees with sum(qty * dim_uom_factor.kg_per_portion) to within 0.04 kg across all 11,747 rows, so never re-apply the factor and never sum qty across ingredient categories, which measures nothing.
definitions.caveat: Read this as an order of magnitude, not a measurement: the whole table is scaled from a single measured day (3.398 kg) by category rates. What does hold is composition -- which cause dominates, and its share of the total -- so compare the parts rather than quoting the whole. Comparing outlets needs one more step: they are not observed for equal periods (365 days at one, 160 at another), so divide by observed days or the least-recorded outlet looks like the thriftiest. Do not present the total as the actual waste of the business, and do not read a trend from it over time. 883.74 kg of the 5,528.50 comes from two ingredient categories whose portion-to-kilogram factor is flagged unusable.

definitions.name: waste_by_cause
definitions.description: Food thrown away, in kilograms, split by the reason it was thrown away. Group by fact_waste.waste_cause. Verified split: prep_trim 2,360.22, spoiled 1,460.13, end_of_day 741.38, plate_return 400.42, over_prep_promo 345.13, delivery_miss 93.39, staff_turnover 70.55, fridge_failure 57.29.
definitions.caveat: Group by waste_cause, never by stage. The two columns share a vocabulary and disagree by up to 30 percent -- prep_trim is 2,634 kg by stage against 2,360 kg by cause -- so the same question answered from the wrong column gives a different number with no sign that anything went wrong. waste_cause is authoritative; stage is retained only for backward compatibility. This split is the most defensible thing in the waste data: the shares hold even though the absolute total does not.

definitions.name: edible_waste
definitions.description: Food thrown away that was still fit to serve at the moment it was discarded, by weight. Verified: 3,005.75 kg of the 5,528.50 kg total, across 6,647 of 11,747 rows. The inedible remainder is 2,522.76 kg.
definitions.caveat: Edible means it was still fit to serve, not that it could realistically have been sold. Trim and preparation loss is largely inherent even where the flag says edible, so this is not a figure of recoverable money and not a target to drive to zero. It inherits the whole-table limit as well: scaled from one measured day, so use it as a share of total waste rather than as an absolute.

definitions.name: waste_intensity
definitions.description: Waste weight per RM1,000 of net sales -- how much food is thrown away relative to how much is sold. Verified: 1.5250 kg per RM1,000, from 5,528.50 kg against RM3,625,180.34. Both tables span 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31.
definitions.caveat: The two halves of this ratio are not equally sound: sales are observed and waste is modelled from a single day, so it is a comparison instrument, not an efficiency measurement. Use it to rank outlets against each other; do not quote it as the waste rate of the business and do not track it over time. Per outlet it must be read per observed day -- coverage runs from 365 days at one outlet to 160 at another, so a straight comparison makes the least-observed outlet look like the thriftiest.
synonyms: waste as a share of sales

definitions.name: net_revenue
definitions.description: Sales after discounts, in ringgit. Verified: RM3,625,180.34 from fact_sale.net_amt, matching the figure in the MiseQ context document to the cent.
definitions.caveat: Revenue comes from fact_sale only. fact_sale_line is a synthetic basket decomposition of those same sales, not a second set of them -- never add the two together, and never treat a line-level total as independent revenue.

definitions.name: observed_waste_days
definitions.description: How many distinct days each outlet actually recorded waste. Verified: 364, 365, 363, 329 and 160 days for outlets 1 to 5.
definitions.caveat: Outlets are not observed for equal periods, and nothing else in the waste data says so. Any per-outlet total or ranking has to be divided by this, or read alongside it -- outlet 5 has 160 observed days against 365 at outlet 2, so on raw totals it looks like the best performer when it is mostly the least recorded.
synonyms: how complete is the waste data
